page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-3200s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with dedicated AMD EPYC processor resources. The server supplies 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware flags including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio with 128 GB of RAM, translating to 8 GB per vCPU. This configuration is paired with 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete GPU accelerators attached. In synthetic evaluations, memory performance ranks in the top tier on PassMark with a score of 2992.99, supported by strong large-block memory bandwidth reaching 340.0 GB/sec for reads and 160.84 GB/sec for writes.

Compute benchmarking shows distinct performance characteristics. The server scores in the top tier for stress-ng single-core performance at 3133.97, while multi-core workloads, such as Geekbench multi-core (13414.0) and PassMark CPU (37621.57), place within the middle tier. In application tests, it handles 38.03 million Redis SET operations per second and reaches 15.74 GB/sec in static web throughput. Without AVX-512 extensions, larger vector workloads are limited, though small-model LLM generation runs at 315.31 tokens per second.

Given its high RAM allocation, fast NVMe capacity, and dedicated core provisioning, the voc-m-16c-128gb-3200s-amd delivers cost-efficient density for storage-heavy and memory-intensive applications. It is suited for relational database clusters, large in-memory key-value caches like Redis, data pipelines, ETL tasks, and write-heavy operational logging.

It features 128 GB of RAM and 3200 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, providing a memory allocation of 8 GB per vCPU without discrete GPU hardware. Hardware benchmark tests demonstrate top-tier single-core stress-ng execution and top-tier PassMark memory performance, backed by 340 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth. Multi-core compute performance remains in the middle range, producing 38.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.74 GB/sec static web throughput. Combining substantial memory density and generous NVMe capacity, this configuration is well matched for memory-resident databases, caching layers, and high-IOPS data processing pipelines.
